verbs.name: render.preview
verbs.description: Fast low-res render of a window starting at at_ms (default 5000ms) for quick agent/human review, OR (draft:true) the incremental whole-timeline draft preview: re-renders only the base-track segments whose inputs changed since the last preview, reuses cached segment files for the rest, and concat-stitches them into one preview mp4 — edit one clip in a 10-clip timeline and only the touched segment re-renders (seconds vs a full ~40s draft render). DERIVED state (cache under proxies/preview-cache/), never an op, never a receipt input — receipts stay render.final.

at_ms.description: Window start (window mode only; REQUIRED unless draft:true). Ignored when draft:true (the preview is the whole timeline).

duration_ms.description: Window length (window mode only). Ignored when draft:true.

draft.description: Incremental whole-timeline draft preview (segment-render cache). When true, at_ms/duration_ms are ignored and the result names which segments re-rendered vs were reused.

verbs.result: {path, mime} window mode; {path, mime, draft:true, segments_rendered, segments_reused, rendered[], reused[], duration_ms} draft mode

verbs.name: render.frame
verbs.description: Compose one frame at at_ms — the agent's eyes / the human scrub frame without a full render. Fast scrub path: by default serves a fast proxy-seek frame (no captions/overlay) scaled to height h; compose:true forces the EXACT composed frame (captions + overlays at project geometry — the agent's verify eyes). Preview frames are bounded to 4K UHD resource limits; use export.frame for an explicit full-resolution still. returns {path, mime}; inline:true adds base64. Raw bytes also at GET /api/frame?at_ms=[&h=][&compose=1] (X-Cut-Frame-Fast header reports the path used).

h.description: scale the frame to this height in px (preview size, up to 2160). Default 540 (the proxy height). Width and total pixels are bounded to a 4K UHD preview budget; use export.frame for an explicit full-resolution still.

compose.description: force the EXACT composed frame (captions + overlays, project geometry) instead of the fast proxy scrub frame. The agent's verify eyes.

verbs.result: {path, mime, at_ms, width, height, fast, base64?}

verbs.name: render.storyboard
verbs.description: Contact sheet: `count` evenly-spaced frames of the composed timeline tiled into a grid image — the agent/judge's see-the-whole-edit-at-a-glance view (one image instead of N frame fetches). Fast proxy-scrub frames by default; compose:true forces exact composed frames (captions/overlays). Single-frame extraction failures are replaced with black placeholder tiles and reported in frame_warnings. Written to the engine-owned frames/ dir.

count.description: Number of frames in the contact sheet (default 12).

compose.description: Force exact composed frames (captions/overlays) instead of fast proxy-scrub.

verbs.result: {path, mime, count, grid:[cols,rows], frame_height, duration_ms, fallback_frames, frame_warnings:[{index,at_ms,code,message,cause}]} (+base64 when inline)

verbs.name: render.reframe
verbs.description: Subject-aware auto-reframe (job, returns {reframe_id, job_id}). Renders the timeline to a temp at project geometry (the finished edit), runs the `subject` perception instrument (local CV: detect+track+saliency -> a normalized, aspect-independent subject track), then a subject-tracked moving-crop POST-PASS to the target aspect. The HONEST replacement for render.final{aspect,fit:cover} (which is a naive STATIC centre-crop that ignores the subject): this FOLLOWS the subject with a smoothed pan, original render untouched. Output default <project>/exports/<reframe_id>.mp4; an explicit fenced path must also end in .mp4. The receipt records subject-in-frame %, the device it analyzed on, and that reframe is a LOSSY crop (not a lossless conversion).

aspect.description: Target aspect ratio W:H with small integers, e.g. 9:16 (vertical), 1:1 (square), 4:5 (portrait), 16:9. Output dimensions are normalized to a 1080-px base, rounded even.

preset.description: Reframe preset: which subject classes to follow + the crop zoom/motion limits. talking_head (person, gentle), sports (person+vehicles, faster motion, less zoom), pets (dog/cat/person), cars (vehicles), general (all classes).

path.description: Optional explicit .mp4 output path (FENCED, canonicalized, no traversal/symlinks, project-or-outputs-dir only). Default <project>/exports/<reframe_id>.mp4.

direction.description: DIRECTOR brief from the foundation model: a per-scene framing decision that OVERRIDES the CV ranker for those scenes. Get the scenes + candidate subjects from render.direct's contact sheet, then map scene index -> the chosen candidate. Shape: {"<scene_idx>": {"cx": <0..1>}} to follow the subject at that normalized x (read each candidate's cx from the contact-sheet JSON), or {"<scene_idx>": {"mode": "widen"}} to hold a centered wide frame. Scenes you omit fall back to the CV ranker. The receipt records which scenes the director decided.

rationale.description: Optional human-readable reason for this reframe (recorded for the operation history; does not affect the output).

verbs.result: {reframe_id, job_id, aspect} — the output path + honesty receipt (subject_in_frame_pct, analyzed_on device, directed_scenes, reframe-is-lossy note) arrive in the job result; render_done event on completion

verbs.name: render.direct
verbs.description: DIRECTOR pass for subject-aware reframe (job): renders the finished edit to a temp and builds a SPARSE per-scene CONTACT SHEET — one annotated keyframe per scene with the candidate subjects labeled A/B/C left->right — for a foundation model to direct the whole clip in one look. The local CV finds and tracks subjects; the model decides which subject each shot is about. Flow: call render.direct -> read the returned contact_sheet image + scenes[].candidates -> decide per scene -> call render.reframe{aspect, direction:{<scene>:{cx}|{mode:'widen'}}}. Omitting the director falls back to the pure CV ranker.

preset.description: Which subject classes to consider as candidates (same set as render.reframe's preset). talking_head = person; sports = person+vehicles; pets = dog/cat/person; cars = vehicles; general = all.

rationale.description: Optional human-readable reason (recorded for the operation history; does not affect the output).

verbs.result: {job_id, direct_id} — the job result carries {contact_sheet (image path to read), scene_count, scenes:[{scene, t_ms, candidates:[{label, cls, cx, cy, box, has_face}]}]}; feed your per-scene pick into render.reframe{direction}

verbs.name: render.qc
verbs.description: DIRECTOR QC pass (job): REVIEW a reframed OUTPUT and decide what to fix. Resolves the actual render.reframe output from receipts/<reframe_id>.json output_path, with legacy fallback to exports/<reframe_id>.mp4. Samples one keyframe per scene of the finished reframe and tiles them into a review sheet WITH cheap CV composition hints per scene — subject_present, face_present, face centering (off_center = |cx-0.5|), headroom (face-top y; a head clipped at the top), and a `needs_review` flag. A foundation model reads the qc_sheet image and for any bad scene re-issue render.reframe{aspect, direction:{<scene>:{cx}|{mode:'widen'}}} with a correction. Closes the director loop: direct -> reframe -> qc -> reframe.

reframe_id.description: The reframe output to review — the reframe_id returned by render.reframe. The actual output is resolved from the reframe receipt output_path, with legacy fallback to exports/<reframe_id>.mp4. Fenced: a bare id, no path separators.

preset.description: Candidate class set for the QC detector (same set as render.reframe's preset).

rationale.description: Optional human-readable reason (recorded for the operation history; does not affect the output).

verbs.result: {job_id, reframe_id} — the job result carries {qc_sheet (image path to read), scene_count, review_count, scenes:[{scene, t_ms, subject_present, face_present, face_cx, off_center, headroom, needs_review, issues}]}; re-issue render.reframe{direction} to fix flagged scenes

verbs.name: render.final
verbs.description: Full deterministic render (job, returns {job_id}). Default path <project>/exports/<render_id>.mp4; an explicit FENCED path must match the chosen container: .mp4 for h264/hevc/av1, .webm for vp9, or .mov for prores. On completion AUTO-runs the output-only RenderChecks battery → RenderReceipt; receipt_ready is always emitted after render_done. The async job result reports verified plus verification_status complete|unmeasured. Optional post-render instrumentation failures preserve verification_error, mark affected receipt rows details.status=unmeasured/details.measured=false, and never create content fix_actions. Long or high-resolution timelines render in adaptive windows internally (segmented) so peak RSS stays bounded regardless of duration — output is byte-identical to a whole-graph render, so deterministic replay is preserved; on Linux each render also runs inside a transient cgroup memory soft-limit (throttle + spill, never a kill). Tune segmentation/footprint via the SHELLX_CUT_RENDER_* env knobs (see SKILL.md / reference.md Runtime knobs).

preset.description: Quality tier (geometry/fps come from project settings): draft = fast review encode (x264 medium CRF 18, AAC 192k), standard = default (x264 slow CRF 20, AAC 192k), high = hero-asset tier (x264 slow CRF 17, AAC 256k). The receipt records the preset used. Within a non-h264 `format` it shifts that codec's rate knob.

format.description: Output FILE FORMAT (codec + container) — 'different file exports'. h264 = universal mp4 + AAC, the default golden combo (byte-identical to omitting format). hevc = H.265 mp4 (Apple hvc1 tag), ~30-50% smaller at equal quality. vp9 = VP9 + Opus.webm, royalty-free web-native. prores = ProRes 422.mov, the pro editing-handoff intermediate. av1 = AV1 mp4, the highest quality ceiling but SOFTWARE-slow here (libsvtav1) — use hardware tier for AV1 speed. The output extension follows the container; `preset` selects the quality tier within the codec.

hardware.description: Encoder tier. auto (default) = use the GPU/hardware encoder when the machine has one (NVENC/QSV/AMF/VideoToolbox) — much faster, and hardware AV1 is the quality ceiling. off = force the software encoder (byte-deterministic, maximum libx264 quality, no GPU). Only h264/hevc/av1 have a hardware tier (vp9/prores are software-only). The hardware encoder is PROBE-VERIFIED with a real test encode, so auto safely falls back to software when no working GPU encoder is present. The receipt's preset field records the encoder that actually ran (e.g. 'standard/hevc_nvenc').

bitrate.description: Target VIDEO bitrate for rate-targeted publishing — e.g. '12M' (12 Mbps), '8000k', or a bare kbps number (50..500000 kbps). Omitted (DEFAULT) = quality-targeted CRF, byte-identical replay. Setting it switches the codec to a real bitrate target (needed to hit a platform spec — see export.publish). Works with the hardware tier (encoder-aware rewrite). ProRes ignores it (profile-fixed).

target_size_mb.description: Target output FILE SIZE in MB — 'fit under X' (Discord 25, email attach, WhatsApp). Computes the video bitrate that keeps the file UNDER the size (from the timeline duration, reserving audio, 90% headroom for VBR variance + container overhead) and renders VBR-under. Mutually exclusive with `bitrate`. Errors if the size is too small for the duration. ProRes ignores it.

rate_control.description: Rate control WHEN bitrate is set. vbr (default) = target AVERAGE, peaks capped ~1.45× for motion headroom; comes in UNDER on simple content (efficient — platform bitrates are ceilings). cbr = TRUE constant bitrate (x264 nal-hrd / x265 strict-cbr pad to the target) for strict-ingest platforms / live streaming. Errors if set without bitrate.

audio_bitrate.description: Target AUDIO bitrate — e.g. '384k' (YouTube), '192k' (social, the default). Omitted = the format's default (192k AAC). Lossless formats (wav, prores PCM) ignore it.

profile.description: Footage profile for the auto-run check battery (profile regression coverage): talking_head = the full strict battery; silent_screen_demo waives lufs/caption_presence/silence_at_edges (recorded as waived_by_profile with the measured outcome kept) and runs a UI-tuned frozen-frame check. NOTE: the uniform_border check `uniform_border` is NOT waived by any profile — a baked-in margin is a defect on screen demos too. The receipt's footage_profile entry records the active profile + auto-detect proposal.

fit.description: Framing fit for sources whose aspect differs from the output frame. contain (DEFAULT, unchanged behavior) = letterbox/pillarbox (scale to fit inside, pad black, no pixels lost). cover = crop-to-fill (scale to cover the frame, centre-crop the overflow). Independent of the quality preset. Omitting it replays byte-identical.

resolution.description: Output geometry. project (DEFAULT, unchanged behavior) = the project settings width×height. match_source = the largest source video geometry on the timeline (a cropped clip contributes its crop rect; fps/audio_rate still come from project settings) — keeps high-res footage at native resolution instead of conforming down. Omitting it replays byte-identical.

aspect.description: Reframe to this aspect for THIS render only (multi-format publish; project untouched): 9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5, etc. Maps to 1080-baseline dims; defaults fit to cover. Mutually exclusive with resolution and width/height.

width.description: Explicit output width px (with height; 16..=7680). Overrides resolution; defaults fit to cover. Mutually exclusive with aspect/resolution.

normalize_loudness.description: Optional target integrated loudness in LUFS. Omitted = no normalization (byte-identical replay). When set, single-pass ffmpeg loudnorm brings the mixed audio to this target (TP -1 dBTP, LRA 11) — closes the measure(lufs check)->target loop. Standard targets: -16 (long-form), -14 (social), -23 (EBU R128).

dry_run.description: When true, return the render PLAN (output geometry, realized duration, per-track manifest, the checks that will run) WITHOUT encoding — verify before a slow render. No job/op/file.

verbs.result: {job_id, render_id} — receipt arrives via receipt_ready / verify.checks

result_schema.x-async-result: shellx-cut://receipts.schema.json#/$defs/RenderReceipt (arrives via receipt_ready / verify.checks; carries checks[] + fix_actions[] for the autopilot self-fix loop)
